text:
maria: Quick idea — create a single waterfall-style chart that stacks latency buckets (p50, p95, p99) alongside unit cost per 1k tokens for our benchmark models. One slide for the webinar landing + a small static for the blog post.

alex: Love it. waterfall + cost overlay sounds clean. can we show both hosted vs dedicated numbers? customers keep asking about predicted cost for production. :eyes: 

maria: Yes, include hosted (avg fleet) and dedicated (reserved) for 3 model families: small, med, large. callouts for where caching / batching cuts cost.

sam: For chart axes, propose left Y = latency (ms), right Y = $/1k tokens. X = model + config (e.g., gpt-small | quant | cached). Labels: p50, p95, p99 stacked markers per variant.

jordan: Suggest we emphasize the tail improvements from smart routing — add a dashed line showing fallback to cheaper variant when latency SLOs miss. helps positioning around graceful degradation.

liv: Copy options for the slide headline: "Latency meets unit economics: what to expect in production" OR "Cutting tail latency without breaking the bank" — which lands better?

alex: Second one feels punchier for webinar signups. shorter headline -> better on social.

sam: Data ask: eng/runtime can we get a table with per-model p50/p95/p99 + $/1k for hosted vs dedicated with and without prefix caching? ideally in CSV. benchbot: I can attach the latest run results, see link: https://bench.internal/runs/649/summary

benchbot: Attached summary csv: run_id=649, models=[redwood-small, redwood-med, open-xl], fields=[p50_ms,p95_ms,p99_ms,cost_per_1k_usd,cache_on].

maria: Nice. Marketing asks for two deliverables: (1) Hero waterfall slide (png + fig for deck) (2) social image (static) + 3 short copy variants for A/B. Also need CTA routing: webinar signups -> enterprise SDR queue if company_size > 200 or if selects "Dedicated" on form. otherwise marketing nurture.

jordan: For routing logic on the form: include a 3-option product interest radio: Hosted / Dedicated / Unsure. If Dedicated -> tag and route to SDR. If Unsure + company size >200 -> route to SDR as well. small startups go to nurture. keep it simple.

liv: Copy variants for social:
- Variant A: "See how smart routing slashes tail latency — and cuts token costs. Join our live demo."
- Variant B: "Faster responses, lower bills: real-world benchmarks from Redwood Inference."
- Variant C: "Production latency vs. price — practical tradeoffs, live walkthrough."
Which should we use for paid ads?

alex: A for paid (action), B for organic (trust), C for webinar description.

sam: Quick mock for slide annotations (paste into figma):
```
X labels: [rs-small, rs-med, open-xl]
For each: bars = {p50: blue, p95: teal, p99: navy}
Overlay line: cost_per_1k (right axis, orange)
Callouts: "Caching -> 2x lower cost" , "Fallback to lightweight model at 99th percentile"
```

jordan: Also add a tiny panel showing hypothetical monthly bill for 10M tokens at each config — converts unit economics to $$ impact. customers like that.

maria: Timeline? we need final assets by Wednesday EOD to sync with webinar invite being sent Thursday morning. Owners: sam = chart + csv prep, liv = copy + social images, alex = landing + signup routing, jordan = CTA logic + SDR link mapping.

sam: Will produce CSV + figma frame by Tuesday. posting a first PNG by EOD Tuesday for review.

liv: I'll write the 3 email subject lines and 6 social variants by Wednesday morning.

alex: I'll update the landing form and add routing tags. ping me if QA needed.

maria: Perfect. small follow-ups: include a single-sentence explainer for the landing under the chart: "We measured latency and unit cost across common model configs — see how batching, caching, and routing change real-world economics."

jordan: FYI: compliance wants a footnote: "Benchmarks run in controlled environment; results may vary by workload." add small gray text.

liv: can someone drop the final copy options in #content-review when ready? i'll shepherd approvals. :pray: 

maria: Thanks team — excited to see the waterfall come together. :rocket:
